name: France
headline: France: +0.9% growth in 2025, 0.9% inflation, debt 116% of GDP
sections: France is a $3.38 trillion economy (2025), the world's 8th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +0.9% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $64K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 9.5% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 0.9% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 5.9% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 7.7% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 18.9% (2025).
Gross government debt is 116% of GDP (2025), a very high level. The general government balance is −5.1% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −0.4% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 67% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.8% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 124% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 83.0 years (2024). Population: 68.9 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
